knowledge_point.title: Differentiating a General Exponential Function Using the Chain Rule

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y={5}^{u},\,u=-2x+{x}^{3}.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}u}={5}^{u}\ln(5),\,\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=-2+3{x}^{2}.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} & =\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}u}\cdot \frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x} \\ & ={5}^{u}\ln(5)\cdot (-2+3{x}^{2}) \\ & =(-2+3{x}^{2})\cdot {5}^{u}\ln(5) \\ & =(-2+3{x}^{2})\cdot {5}^{-2x+{x}^{3}}\ln(5).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=-1$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ at that point as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m=\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\big|_{x=-1} & =(-2+3(-1)^{2})\cdot {5}^{-2(-1)+(-1)^{3}}\ln(5) \\ & =1\cdot {5}^{1}\ln(5) \\ & =5 \ln{\left(5 \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point where $x=-1$ is $5 \ln{\left(5 \right)}.$
